page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features an arm64 CPU architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance does not utilize hyperthreading, allocating exactly one thread per physical core, and is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor system.

This instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, providing high-speed local block storage directly attached to the host. It does not feature any graphics processing units.

The c9gd.xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The primary tradeoff of this instance profile is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2:1, which limits its use for memory-intensive applications. Additionally, workloads must be compatible with the arm64 instruction set, and there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Given its compute-focused design and local NVMe storage, this instance is structured for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles and fast local scratch space. Suitable workloads include distributed build systems, log processing, media encoding, and application servers that require high compute density relative to memory capacity.
